Read chromatograms from UNICORN 6 and later

Source: R/read_akta.R
chrom_read_akta_result.Rd

ÄKTA systems run by UNICORN 6 and later save each run as a result, which UNICORN can export as a .zip archive or as curves in a .csv file.

  • chrom_read_akta_result() reads a result archive, the .zip file from "Export" in UNICORN's Evaluation module. It needs the xml2 package.

  • chrom_read_akta_csv() reads curves exported to a .csv file.

Each trace is recorded at its own volumes. The traces are combined into one row per volume of the UV trace, and the other traces are interpolated onto those volumes. The fraction marks give the fraction of each row; rows before the first mark, or after a mark such as "Waste", have no fraction. The run log and injection marks are dropped.

For exports from UNICORN 5 and earlier, see read_akta_old().

Usage

chrom_read_akta_result(file)

chrom_read_akta_csv(file)

Arguments

file

Path to the .zip result or .csv export.

Value

A chromatogram: a tibble with the run's metadata, see chrom_meta(). Results record the run's name and when it was created.

Columns

The readers all give one row per sampled point, with the columns the instrument recorded:

  • time, in seconds, when the instrument records it, and volume, in mL.

  • fraction, the fraction each row was collected into, or NA when it wasn't collected.

  • Absorbance, named after its wavelength in nm, such as a280, or uv when the instrument doesn't record the wavelength.

  • The other traces under standard names: conductivity, conductivity_percent, percent_b, pressure, flow and temperature.

fraction is a fraction vector and the absorbance columns are absorbance vectors, which record their wavelength and unit. The other columns are quantity vectors with the unit recorded in the file, such as s, mL, mS/cm, psi or MPa.

Examples

fl <- system.file("extdata", "example_akta_3.csv", package = "chromr")
chrom_read_akta_csv(fl)
#> # A chromatogram: 9,572 × 2
#> # Instrument:     ÄKTA
#>    volume    uv
#>      <mL> <mAU>
#>  1  0.224  2.02
#>  2  0.237  2.03
#>  3  0.25   2.05
#>  4  0.264  2.06
#>  5  0.277  2.1 
#>  6  0.29   2.12
#>  7  0.304  2.16
#>  8  0.317  2.21
#>  9  0.33   2.25
#> 10  0.344  2.30
#> # ℹ 9,562 more rows
